regime: Hawkish Fed tightening + 5% Treasury hurdle + adaptive but still impaired Middle East energy logistics
whatIsNewNow: Fed raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16; 16 of 18 policymakers expect at least one more hike by year-end and futures imply about 90% odds of another 25bp hike.
Post-Fed US 2Y finished about 4.738% and 10Y 5.00%; dollar index rose to 100.31, gold fell to about $4,263/oz and equities weakened.

Energy scarcity became more adaptive: Saudi Arabia is offering extra crude to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, Oman. Brent fell 2.69% to $105.83, but Hormuz vessel passage remains constrained.

US LNG rerouting strengthened structurally: Equinor plans to grow LNG supply to 10-15 mtpa in the early 2030s and is already lifting US LNG from Cheniere; QatarEnergy continues seeking 2-3 mtpa of US supply through 2031.
Singapore August exports surged 46.2% y/y with AI demand an important driver, fresh evidence that physical electronics/AI trade remains strong despite tighter financial conditions.
whatMattersMostNow: 1. Capital scarcity / Fed hiking cycle and 5% long-end yields
2. Middle East refined products/shipping with partial rerouting adaptation
3. Funded AI power/grid/cooling demand and cash conversion
5. AI memory/HBM scarcity and strategic localization
10. ESS deployment versus battery manufacturing overcapacity
